text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Two car bombs explode just 10 minutes apart in the spa resort of Sidi Bouhanifia in the western province of Mascara killing 15 people and wounding 23. One blast destroyed Sahara hotel in the town while another hotel was badly damaged. Among the wounded a child, who was hit seriously in the head, had his hand amputated. One hospital source said half of the dead could not be identified.

- The government-appointed Transitional National Council, convenes on Sunday to study a retirement bill. The government draft suggests cutting the retirement age to try to trim the number of employees in the government bureaucracy.
- Algeria's Gross Domestic Product growth was 4.0 percent in 1996 thanks to surging crude oil prices and a brisk hydrocarbon sub-sector.
- Political parties plot their election strategy for the impending poll campaign.
- President Liamine Zeroual says economic reforms were necessary to pull the country out of a deep crisis and were not forced on Algeria by the International Monetary Fund.
